# @rachel_rotenberg/ai-contribution-tracker

Tags git commits made after AI work with an `Impacted by AI (...)` marker. One package for:

| Host | Version | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode 1.x | 1.18.29 or newer (tested on 1.19.5) | `index.ts` (`server`) |
| OpenCode 2.x | tested on 2.2.5 | `index.ts` (`setup`) |
| OmO Native (`omo`, senpi engine) | tested on omo 5.1.62 | `senpi.ts` (pi package manifest) |

## Install

### OpenCode 1.x and 2.x (macOS and Windows)

Add the package **once**, under `plugin`, in your OpenCode config
(`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`; on Windows `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\opencode.json`):

```json
{ "plugin": ["@rachel_rotenberg/ai-contribution-tracker"] }
```

Both majors read the `plugin` key, so one entry covers both. Do not also add it under OpenCode 2's
`plugins` key: 2.x then loads it twice (the tracker ignores the second copy, but there is no reason to have it).
`npx @rachel_rotenberg/ai-contribution-tracker init` writes this entry and installs the git hooks for you;
the VS Code extension does the same automatically.

### OmO Native

```sh
omo install npm:@rachel_rotenberg/ai-contribution-tracker
```

The package carries a `pi` manifest (`"pi": { "extensions": ["./senpi.ts"] }`), so `omo` loads only the OmO
extension from it. To try it for one run without installing: `omo -e npm:@rachel_rotenberg/ai-contribution-tracker`.

### Git hooks

On first load each host installs a global `core.hooksPath` (`~/.config/ai-contribution-tracker/git-hooks`
unless you already have one) with a `prepare-commit-msg` stamp block and a `post-commit` block. Hooks are
`#!/bin/sh` scripts; on Windows they run in Git for Windows' bundled `sh.exe`. Repo-local hooks
(`.git/hooks/*`, Husky, LFS) keep running through delegating stubs. `npx @rachel_rotenberg/ai-contribution-tracker remove`
uninstalls them.

## What is reported

```
Impacted by AI (Agent mode: opencode/build | Model: claude-sonnet-4-6 | Prompts: 2 | Sub-agents mode: explore | sub-Agent prompts: 1 | Tokens: claude-sonnet-4-6: 41k in/1k out (38k cached))
Co-authored-by: OpenCode (claude-sonnet-4-6, 2p) <noreply@opencode.dev>
```

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| Agent mode | `opencode/<agent>` (OpenCode 1/2), `omo/main` (OmO) |
| Model | models of the main agent |
| Prompts | user prompts of the main agent (subagent and injected prompts excluded) |
| Sub-agents mode / sub-Agent prompts | subagent types and count of subagent tool calls (`task` on OpenCode 1 and OmO, `subagent` on OpenCode 2) |
| Tokens | per model, main agent only: `in` = input + cache read, `cached` = cache read, `+N reasoning`; `model: unknown tokens` when the host reported no usage |

The repo is picked from the paths the agent's tools touch, never from the directory the host was started in,
so a session opened in a parent folder of several repos stamps the repo actually edited. A subagent that works
in another repo stamps that repo with the root agent and subagent type.

## Known limits

- OpenCode 1.x older than 1.18.29 does not accept object plugin entries; use plugin 1.0.x there.
- Two processes writing the same repo's state at the same instant can lose one update (writes are atomic, so the
  file is never corrupted; the loss is bounded to one event).
- Subagent tokens are not counted (same as 1.0.x).
- `in` does not include cache writes (same as 1.0.x).
- OmO task children run in OmO's task host, apart from the parent. A child cannot see its category, so a commit whose
  only AI work came from a child reads `Sub-agents mode: task` with no prompt or token counts (the parent's turn never
  touched a file). When the parent also edits files, the real category and the parent's counts are reported.
- `-e`/`--extension` loads the OmO extension in the main session only; install it (`omo install`) so task children load it too.
- Work done before any tool touches a file in a repo is kept in memory only; if the host exits first it is lost.

# Changelog

## 1.1.0

### Added
- OpenCode 2.x support (`setup` entry next to the 1.x `server` entry, one default export).
- OmO Native (omo / senpi) support via `senpi.ts` and a `pi` package manifest.
- Package tests (`npm test`) driven by event payloads recorded from OpenCode 1.19.5, OpenCode 2.2.5 and omo 5.1.62.

### Fixed
- OpenCode 1.19: markers showed `Agent mode: opencode/session` and no `Model:` because 1.19 sends the agent and
  model only on `chat.message`'s output message. Both are read from there now.
- Usage reported before the agent's first file touch (including the first turn on OmO, whose assistant message
  ends before its tools run) was dropped while the prompts of that turn were counted. It is buffered like prompts.
- A usage snapshot that dipped and recovered was counted twice; each message/step now counts its highest value once.
- A torn read of `ai-tracker-state.json` during a concurrent write reset the repo's state. Writes are atomic
  (temp file + rename), and a corrupted file is logged once instead of silently discarded.
- After a commit, seeing `AI_IMPACT_CONSUMED` deleted state that another host had just written.
- Rebase: replayed commits could be stamped with, and consume, a pending marker. Both hook blocks now skip rebases.
- Windows: hook delegation treated `C:/...` from `git rev-parse` as relative, so repo-local hooks were skipped
  in worktrees. Hook files with CRLF are normalized; `core.hooksPath` is set without a shell.
- A session first seen mid-stream (host restart) is classified as main or subagent by asking the host.
- A subagent spawned before the agent touched any file (common on OmO, where the root often only delegates) was not
  counted. It is buffered like prompts. An unknown subagent type (`task`) gives way to a concrete one in the same commit.

### Changed
- Plugin `post-commit` block is now a managed block (upgraded in place on load).
- Requires OpenCode 1.18.29 or newer on 1.x (object plugin entries).
